content:
The image shows a split-open soybean pod with:
- Dense **white, cottony/fluffy mycelium** filling the inside of the pod
- The seed inside is covered in this white fungal growth
- Pod walls are darkened/blackened
- The mycelium has that characteristic loose, woolly texture

This is a textbook presentation of **White Mold** (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum). The defining feature is the dense white cottony mycelium inside the pod cavity — this is one of the most recognizable symptoms, distinct from other diseases. No other class produces this internal pod mycelium with this specific white, fluffy texture.
